angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 335,327 km at 191.14 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.2318 +/- 0.0222 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 191.14 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.482 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Rowe et al. 2014, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-249 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...784...45R/abstract): 335,327 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.510238 +/- 0.020399 solar masses from TICv8, the stellar mass of Kepler-249 c's parameter set from TICv8 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3568 +/- 150 K from Rowe et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-249 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...784...45R/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Rowe et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-249 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...784...45R/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-249.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.780, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
